questions.q: Per the consolidated checklist, what should never be accepted as proof that MFA exists for a population of users?
options: Session Security Level configuration
A documented MFA policy signed by the client
A direct verification that the external IdP enforces MFA
The statement 'we use SSO' alone, without separately verifying MFA enforcement at the IdP
questions.explain: As emphasized throughout the course, SSO does not automatically imply MFA — the architect must directly verify MFA enforcement, whether through Salesforce's own requirement or at the external IdP.

questions.q: What does it mean for an identity architecture to 'fail safely'?
options: When something goes wrong (an outage, a leaked token, a mistake), the resulting damage is limited and contained rather than cascading broadly
It automatically disables all user access during any error
It relies entirely on manual intervention for every failure
It never experiences any failures at all
questions.explain: Failing safely means a break-glass admin path survives an IdP outage, a leaked token's damage is limited by minimal scope, and similar properties — containment of failure, not its total absence.

questions.q: Why does the review checklist specifically call for auditing Named Credentials for Per-User vs. Named Principal usage?
options: Because this only matters for inbound SSO, not outbound callouts
Because Named Credentials are irrelevant to security
Because using Named Principal where external accountability is actually required silently erases which individual Salesforce user triggered an outbound call
Because Per-User is always wrong and should be replaced with Named Principal
questions.explain: As covered in Lesson 19, using Named Principal when per-user accountability is actually needed on the external system defeats that accountability — worth checking explicitly during a security review.

questions.q: Why does the lesson recommend interviewing the client's team about their actual offboarding process, rather than relying only on documentation?
options: Interviews are a legal requirement for every Salesforce project
Offboarding processes never involve any identity-related risk
Documentation is always perfectly accurate and interviews are unnecessary
Most real identity security gaps are found in the difference between what a runbook says should happen and what actually happens during a rushed, real-world termination
questions.explain: The lesson notes that the gap between documented process and real-world practice, especially under the time pressure of an actual termination, is where most practical identity security gaps are actually found.

questions.q: According to the lesson, what almost always separates a secure identity architecture from a merely functional one?
options: Discipline in details like scope minimization, tested break-glass paths, and prompt deactivation propagation, rather than protocol sophistication alone
Having the largest possible number of Connected Apps
Avoiding Multi-Factor Authentication entirely to reduce complexity
Using the newest, most advanced protocol available regardless of context
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly states the difference is almost never about more advanced protocols — it's about disciplined attention to the specific details (scopes, break-glass paths, deactivation propagation) covered throughout the course.
